key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage concentrated near the buried hole-transport-layer interface in p-i-n perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: This approach enables rapid screening of interface treatments to improve perovskite device stability without destructive sectioning.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe degradation at different depths.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL, and ideality-factor measurements under UV soaking.
Compare perovskite films and devices with different ITO interface modifiers.
evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements localize preferential interface degradation consistently with ex-situ destructive tests and show reduced UV damage with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative stability gains or validation beyond UV soaking, so broader operational durability remains to be established.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
